images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of PhyCoVE.The three shapes in the center stand for the three materials, an overlap of two shapes marks the interaction pattern of those materials, and the rigid-rigid and elastic-elastic patterns lie in single shapes. The panels show example scenes and case counts of the five patterns, and the bottom row shows the three edit types and an edit at a later execution frame.
Figure 2:Representative cases from PhyCoVE.Each case pairs a source video and a physical edit at its execution frame with a counterfactual target video.

Figure 3:Construction of the simulated set.A language model proposes scene designs, coding agents build the selected designs into source scenes, we simulate each edit from its execution frame, and humans check the result of every stage.

Figure 7:Qualitative comparison.Each block shows one case with the CF of each generated video, and the third case comes from the real set. Videos that miss the edit keep the toy car afloat after removing the float, change the color of the wine instead of its flow rate, or leave the ball at the bottom of the mug after adding water.

Figure S3:Removals.Each block shows one case with the CF of each generated video, and the second case comes from the real set. In the target videos, the soccer ball disappears at frame 49, and the ping-pong ball hits the tissue packet instead of the paddle.

Figure S4:Changes of a physical quantity.Each block shows one case with the CF of each generated video. In the target videos, the denser water lifts the toy car and the rock to the surface, and the softer core lets the duck sag under the water stream.

Figure S5:Insertions.Each block shows one case with the CF of each generated video. In the target videos, the falling book lands on the inserted book, and the car stops in front of the two bottles, which stay upright.
